mainTopic: Repaying eaten תרומה by measure or by value, and whether תרומה of חמץ on פסח has value that must be repaid
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: even one who anoints with תרומה oil pays a חומש, and if he uses up that חומש he pays a חומש of the חומש. The גמרא then asks whether eaten תרומה is repaid by the amount eaten (לפי מדה) or by its money value (לפי דמים). If the price dropped, he clearly pays the higher original value, like a גזלן. The real question is when the price rose. רב יוסף tries to prove 'by measure' from a ברייתא that praises one who repays dried figs with dates, but אביי explains that the praise is for paying with a fruit that sells easily. Our משנה obligates one who accidentally eats תרומה of חמץ on פסח to pay. The גמרא shows this can fit 'by value' if the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who permits benefit from חמץ on פסח, together with רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, who exempts a deliberate כרת act from payment. Finally, two ברייתות record תנאים arguing over whether one who eats תרומת חמץ on פסח must pay. Each debate centers on whether such חמץ has any permitted use, such as burning it for fuel.

steps.title: Anointing with תרומה oil also requires a חומש, and even a חומש of the חומש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that one who anoints with תרומה oil, whether טמאה or טהורה, pays a חומש, and also a חומש of the חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also one who anoints himself with תרומה oil, whether it is impure תרומה or pure תרומה, pays an extra fifth, and also a fifth of the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about someone who used תרומה by mistake. It adds that anointing counts like eating, and that this applies to both pure and impure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סיכה (anointing) is treated like drinking, so it also brings the obligation of קרן plus חומש. Including תרומה טמאה is a real addition, because impure תרומה cannot be eaten anyway, yet using it still obligates a חומש. 'חומשא דחומשא' teaches that the חומש paid takes on the status of תרומה, so using it by mistake creates a new חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: One who anoints (rubs oil on his body)
The extra 'fifth' added when repaying תרומה eaten by mistake
A fifth of the fifth: if one uses up the paid fifth, he must add a fifth on it too
Ritually impure תרומה, which may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think impure תרומה is free to use because it is 'already ruined.' It is still תרומה, and using it by mistake still requires a חומש.

phrases.english: And likewise one who anoints himself (with terumah oil),
whether it is impure terumah
or pure terumah —
he pays an additional fifth
and a fifth of the fifth.
phrases.notes: The paid חומש itself has תרומה status, so consuming it by mistake brings another חומש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶחָד הַסָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud about payment for תרומה used by mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anointing with תרומה, pure or impure, obligates a חומש, and using the חומש obligates a חומש of the חומש.

steps.title: Does one repay תרומה by amount or by money value?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises an איבעיא: is repayment for eaten תרומה measured by quantity (לפי מדה) or by money value (לפי דמים)?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: When he pays, does he pay according to the amount he ate, or according to its money value?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how the payment for תרומה is calculated. It is setting up a discussion that will narrow down exactly when this question matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible ways to measure repayment: return the same quantity of produce, or return its money worth. The two give different results only when prices change between eating and paying.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars (a genuine dilemma, which the גמרא then tries to resolve)
According to the measure, i.e. the same quantity
According to the money value

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
When he pays,
does he pay according to the measure
or does he pay according to the money value?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the payment obligation in the ברייתא and asks how that payment is calculated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether repayment for eaten תרומה follows quantity or money value.

steps.title: When the price went down, he clearly pays the original value, like a thief
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the question: if the תרומה dropped in value from four זוזים to one, he certainly pays the original value, because he is no better off than a גזלן, who pays according to the time of the theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever it was worth four זוזים at first and in the end was worth one זוז, you have no question. He certainly pays according to the original money value, because he is no better than a thief. As we learned in a משנה: All thieves pay according to the value at the time of the theft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which case is not in doubt, which prepares us to see the case that really is in doubt. If the price fell, he pays the higher original value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'paying by measure' would let him pay only one זוז, which would be cheaper than what he took. Someone who ate תרומה should not do better than a גזלן, and a גזלן pays the value at the time of the theft. So in this case paying the original money value is obvious, and the משנה is cited as support.

keyTerms.meaning: At the beginning (here: at the time he ate it)
Don't ask; this case is not in doubt
A thief who takes openly or by force
According to the value at the time of the theft

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the real question is not about protecting the eater from a loss. It is only about whether he must pay more when the price went up.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא שָׁוְיָא אַרְבְּעָה זוּזֵי
phrases.english: Wherever it was worth four zuz at the outset
and at the end it was worth one zuz —
you need not ask,
for certainly he pays according to the original money value,
because he is no worse than a thief.
As we learned in a mishnah:
All thieves pay according to the time of the theft.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא שָׁוְיָא אַרְבְּעָה זוּזֵי וּלְבַסּוֹף שָׁוְיָא זוּזָא לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the איבעיא by removing the case of falling prices from doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the value fell, he pays the original value, as a גזלן pays according to the time of the theft.

steps.title: The real question: when the price went up
steps.stepSummary: The real doubt is when the value rose from one זוז to four. Does he pay the same quantity ('you ate a סאה, pay a סאה'), or the original money value ('you ate a זוז's worth, pay a זוז')?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where you can ask is when it was worth one זוז at first and in the end worth four. What is the law? Does he pay by amount, since the כהן can say to him, 'You ate a סאה, you pay a סאה'? Or perhaps he pays by money value: he ate a זוז's worth, he pays a זוז's worth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the exact case in doubt: the price rose between eating and paying. It lays out both sides of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying by measure means returning a full סאה, which now costs four זוזים. Paying by value means returning only one זוז's worth. Now the two methods really lead to different results, and the eater is the one who would lose under 'measure'.

keyTerms.meaning: A סאה, a unit of dry volume
A זוז, a silver coin
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a doubt)
What (is the law)?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the previous case. Here the price went up, so 'paying by measure' is the stricter option, not the more lenient one.

phrases.english: Where you can raise the dilemma
is where at the outset it was worth one zuz
and at the end it was worth four — what is the law?
Does he pay according to measure,
since (the kohen) can say to him:
phrases.notes: That's the כהן, the one who is owed the payment.

phrases.english: 'You ate a se'a — you pay a se'a.'
Or perhaps he pays according to money value:
he ate a zuz's worth — he pays a zuz's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא שָׁוְיָא זוּזָא וּלְבַסּוֹף שָׁוְיָא אַרְבְּעָה מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out the falling-price case, presents the rising-price case as the true doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the price rose, must he return the same quantity (now worth more) or only the original money value?

steps.title: רב יוסף cites a ברייתא: paying dates for figs earns a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא: one who ate תרומה dried figs and repaid with dates, may a blessing come upon him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Come and hear: If someone ate dried figs and paid him back with dates, may a blessing come upon him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source to try to answer the question. In this step he only quotes the ברייתא, and the next step explains how it proves something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates are worth more than dried figs. The ברייתא praises someone who repays with the more valuable fruit, and רב יוסף will argue that this praise only makes sense under one side of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Dried figs (cheaper)
Dates (more expensive)
May a blessing come upon him (praise for doing more than required)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Come and hear:
If one ate dried figs (of terumah)
and paid him back with dates,
may a blessing come upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source to resolve the איבעיא from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The question of whether payment is by measure or by value.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא praising one who ate dried figs and repaid with dates.

steps.title: The blessing only makes sense if payment is by measure
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains: if payment is by measure, he ate a סאה of figs worth one זוז and gave a סאה of dates worth four, so he deserves a blessing. If payment is by value, he paid exactly what he owed, a זוז for a זוז, so why a blessing?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say he pays by measure. That is why a blessing should come upon him: he ate a סאה of dried figs worth one זוז and gave a סאה of dates worth four. But if you say he pays by money value, why should a blessing come upon him? He ate a זוז's worth and he pays a זוז's worth!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף spells out his proof: the ברייתא's praise fits only the view that one pays by measure. So he concludes that payment is לפי מדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under 'measure,' he returns one סאה but chose an expensive fruit, giving more than required, which deserves praise. Under 'value,' he must give only one זוז's worth anyway, so a smaller amount of dates is just ordinary payment with nothing special about it. Therefore the ברייתא seems to support paying by measure.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (if you say...), introducing the side that fits
Because of this, for this reason
Why?

steps.whatToRemember: The איבעיא only matters when the price rose. רב יוסף tries to prove from 'dates for figs earns a blessing' that one pays לפי מדה, the same quantity, because under לפי דמים there would be nothing praiseworthy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main proof offered for paying by measure. The גמרא will examine whether the ברייתא could be explained another way.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לְפִי מִדָּה מְשַׁלֵּם —
phrases.english: Granted, if you say he pays according to measure —
that is why a blessing should come upon him,
for he ate a se'a of dried figs worth one zuz,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא יָהֵיב גְּרִיוָא דִתְמָרִים דְּשָׁוְיָא אַרְבְּעָה.
phrases.english: and he gives a se'a of dates worth four.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְפִי דָמִים מְשַׁלֵּם —
phrases.english: But if you say he pays according to money value —
why should a blessing come upon him?
He ate a zuz's worth — and he pays a zuz's worth!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לְפִי מִדָּה מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 5 resolves the איבעיא.
steps.raayaObject: That payment for eaten תרומה is לפי מדה (by quantity).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's blessing is meaningful only if a full סאה is owed, so that giving dates means giving more than required.

steps.title: אביי: The blessing is for paying with a more sellable fruit
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof. Even if payment is by value, the payer earns a blessing because he paid with dates, which buyers grab, instead of dried figs, which buyers ignore.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, he pays by money value. So why should a blessing come upon him? Because he ate something buyers don't jump at, and he paid with something buyers do jump at.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof. He shows that the ברייתא's blessing still makes sense even if payment is by value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed a blessing only makes sense if the כהן received more value. אביי says the כהן can gain even at equal value: dates are easy to resell, while dried figs are hard to sell. So the ברייתא no longer proves 'by measure'.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (used to hold on to a position despite the challenge)
May a blessing come upon him
Jumps at it (eagerly wanted)
Its buyers

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the dates are worth more money. In his case both fruits are worth the same. The only difference is how easy each one is to sell.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם לְפִי דָמִים מְשַׁלֵּם,
phrases.english: Abaye said: Really, he pays according to value,
and why should a blessing come upon him?
phrases.notes: אביי restates רב יוסף's question so he can answer it.

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲכַל מִידֵּי דְּלָא קָפֵיץ עֲלֵיהּ זָבֹינֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Because he ate something that buyers don't jump at (dried figs),

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מְשַׁלֵּם מִידֵּי דְּקָפֵיץ עֲלֵיהּ זָבֹינֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and he pays with something that buyers do jump at (dates).
phrases.notes: Same value, but easier for the כהן to sell.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם לְפִי דָמִים מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof from the ברייתא of figs and dates.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove the opposite view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The blessing can be explained by how easily the fruit sells, not by higher value.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: חמץ on פסח has no value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings our משנה: one who accidentally eats תרומה of חמץ on פסח pays קרן וחומש. Payment by measure fits this. Payment by value does not seem to work, because חמץ on פסח is worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: One who eats תרומה of חמץ on פסח by accident pays the principal plus a fifth. If you say he pays by measure, fine. But if you say he pays by value, does חמץ on פסח have any value?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the question using our own משנה. It argues that the 'by value' approach cannot explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ on פסח is normally forbidden for any benefit (אסור בהנאה), so it is worth nothing. If payment is by value, the eater should owe nothing. Yet the משנה says he pays קרן וחומש, which suggests payment is by measure.

keyTerms.meaning: By accident / unknowingly
The principal plus an added fifth
Granted / it works well if
Something that has monetary value

phrases.english: We learned: One who eats תרומה of chametz on Pesach,
if by accident, pays the principal and a fifth.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לְפִי מִדָּה מְשַׁלֵּם — שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: Granted, if you say he pays by measure, it works well.
phrases.notes: He ate a סאה, so he pays a סאה, regardless of value.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לְפִי דָמִים מְשַׁלֵּם,
phrases.english: But if you say he pays by value,
does chametz on Pesach have any value?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: it seems to be worth nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמַת חָמֵץ בַּפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new proof from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that payment is by value (לפי דמים).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Worthless חמץ on פסח would mean nothing is owed, yet the משנה requires קרן וחומש.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, so the חמץ has value
steps.stepSummary: Yes, the חמץ has value, because the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who permits benefit from חמץ on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it has value. Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said that benefit from חמץ on פסח is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 'by value' approach. It says the משנה follows a תנא for whom חמץ on פסח is not worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, חמץ on פסח may not be eaten but may be used or sold for benefit. So it keeps real monetary value, and paying 'by value' makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Whose view is this?
Permitted for benefit

phrases.aramaic: אִין, הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא,
phrases.english: Yes, whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who said chametz on Pesach is permitted for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חמץ on פסח is worthless, so payment must be by measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי הגלילי the חמץ has value, so payment by value still works.

steps.title: Challenge from the end of the משנה: Why is the deliberate eater exempt?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, why does the end of the משנה exempt a deliberate eater from all payment, even the value of the חמץ as firewood?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: if he ate it on purpose, he is exempt from payment and even from the value of firewood. If this is רבי יוסי הגלילי, why is he exempt from payment and from the value of firewood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It uses the end of the same משנה to do so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חמץ has value, then a person who deliberately ate someone else's תרומה destroyed something valuable. He should at least pay for the loss, like any damager, even if he skips the added fifth. The total exemption seems to show the חמץ is worthless, which contradicts רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Say (look at) the end clause
On purpose / deliberately
Its value as firewood (fuel)

steps.confusionAlert: 'דמי עצים' means even the minimal value of the חמץ as fuel for burning. The משנה exempts him from paying even that small amount.

phrases.english: If so, say the end clause:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמֵזִיד פָּטוּר מִן הַתַּשְׁלוּמִין וּמִדְּמֵי עֵצִים,
phrases.english: If on purpose, he is exempt from payment and from the value of firewood,
if it is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי פָּטוּר מִן הַתַּשְׁלוּמִין וּמִדְּמֵי עֵצִים?!
phrases.english: why is he exempt from payment and from the value of firewood?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חמץ has value, the deliberate eater should have to pay for destroying it.

steps.title: The משנה also follows רבי נחוניא בן הקנה
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of the משנה also holds like רבי נחוניא בן הקנה. He treated יום הכיפורים like שבת regarding payment: an act punishable by כרת exempts from money payment. Eating חמץ on פסח carries כרת, so the deliberate eater pays nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, as it was taught: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה used to treat יום הכיפורים like שבת regarding payments, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The exemption comes from a separate rule, not from the חמץ being worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that one who commits an act deserving a death penalty is exempt from paying for damage done in that same act. רבי נחוניא בן הקנה extends this to acts punishable by כרת, like יום הכיפורים. Deliberately eating חמץ on פסח carries כרת, so the deliberate eater is exempt, even though the חמץ has value.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (another view)
Regarding payments

steps.whatToRemember: The 'by value' view survives both attacks. אביי explained the figs-and-dates blessing as being about how easily the fruit sells. The חמץ משנה works as רבי יוסי הגלילי (the חמץ has value) combined with רבי נחוניא בן הקנה (a כרת act exempts from payment).
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows the גמרא may attribute one משנה to a combination of two תנאים' views in order to defend a reading.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה.
phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana.
As it was taught: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה אֶת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כַּשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: would treat Yom Kippur like Shabbat
regarding payments, etc.
phrases.notes: Violating שבת carries a death penalty, which exempts from payment. יום הכיפורים carries כרת, and he treats it the same way.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a second תנא's principle to explain the exemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The deliberate eater's exemption shows the חמץ is worthless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption comes from the כרת rule of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, not from worthlessness.

steps.title: The question matches a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that the measure-versus-value question is like a מחלוקת תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא exempts one who eats תרומת חמץ on פסח, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי obligates him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: One who eats תרומה of חמץ on פסח is exempt from payment, and even from paying its value as firewood. These are the words of רבי עקיבא. רבי יוחנן בן נורי obligates him to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the earlier question to an older dispute between תנאים. It then quotes a ברייתא that shows two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא exempts the eater because חמץ on פסח is worth nothing, which fits payment by value. רבי יוחנן בן נורי obligates him, which fits payment by measure, since a measure of food can always be repaid. So the earlier question turns out to be an old מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים; this question was already argued about by them
תרומה that is חמץ, meaning leavened grain
The value of something as firewood
Holds him liable to pay

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says the words 'measure' or 'value.' The גמרא is reading those two positions into this dispute: the one who exempts holds 'value,' and the one who obligates holds 'measure.'

phrases.english: It is like a dispute of Tannaim:
phrases.notes: Links the measure-vs-value question to a מחלוקת תנאים

phrases.english: One who eats teruma of chametz on Pesach
is exempt from payment and from its value as firewood,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri holds him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the משנה, the גמרא shows that the measure-versus-value question is itself a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of paying by measure or by value is disputed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks what benefit there is
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי יוחנן בן נורי: what benefit does חמץ on פסח have, that the eater should pay for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to רבי יוחנן בן נורי: What benefit is there in it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא challenges the other opinion. He argues that חמץ on פסח is useless, so there is nothing to pay for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one may get any benefit from חמץ on פסח, so the כהן lost nothing of value. If payment matches the loss, the payment should be zero.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit or use
'But what...?', the opening of a challenge

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּהּ?
phrases.english: But what benefit is there for him in it?
phrases.notes: חמץ on פסח is forbidden for any benefit

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא gives the reason behind his ruling in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling that the eater must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something with no permitted use has no value, so there is nothing to repay.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי points to impure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי answers: impure תרומה cannot be eaten either, yet one who eats it during the year still pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said to רבי עקיבא: What benefit is there in impure תרומה during the rest of the year? Yet one who eats it pays!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן נורי answers the challenge with a comparison. Impure תרומה also cannot be eaten, and still the eater must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues that payment does not depend on whether the food is usable. Impure תרומה is forbidden to eat, but the eater pays anyway. So the same should apply to חמץ on פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה that became impure; a כהן may not eat it
He pays

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said to Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה
phrases.english: And what benefit is there for one who eats impure teruma
during all the rest of the days of the year, yet he pays!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's challenge with a parallel case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case (impure תרומה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Food with no permitted use needs no payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Impure תרומה cannot be eaten yet requires payment, so lack of use does not cancel payment.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says impure תרומה can be burned, but חמץ cannot
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the comparison. Impure תרומה may be burned for fuel, but חמץ on פסח has no use at all. It is like impure berries and grapes, which can be neither eaten nor burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No! You may say this about impure תרומה during the year. Even though it may not be eaten, it may be burned for fuel. Will you say the same here, where it may be neither eaten nor burned? What is this case similar to? To תרומה of berries and grapes that became impure, which may be neither eaten nor burned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back. He shows that impure תרומה is different from חמץ on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure תרומה still has a use: a כהן may burn it for heat, so it has some value. חמץ on פסח has no permitted use at all. A better comparison is impure berries and grapes, which are too wet to burn and so are completely useless.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No! If you say...', the formula for rejecting a comparison
Permission to burn it for fuel
Permission to eat it
Berries and grapes; too moist to serve as fuel

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows רבי עקיבא's view clearly: payment depends on whether the item had any permitted use at all. That fits the 'value' approach.

phrases.english: He said to him: No!

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִּתְרוּמָה טְמֵאָה בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: If you say so about impure teruma during the rest of the year,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה,
phrases.english: that even though he has no permission to eat it,
he has permission to burn it,
will you say so about this,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ לֹא הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה וְלֹא הֶיתֵּר הַסָּקָה!
phrases.english: where he has neither permission to eat it nor permission to burn it!
Rather, what is this similar to?
To teruma of berries and grapes that became impure,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ לֹא הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה וְלֹא הֶיתֵּר הַסָּקָה.
phrases.english: where he has neither permission to eat it nor permission to burn it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא! אִם אָמַרְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוחנן בן נורי's comparison to impure תרומה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between impure תרומה and חמץ on פסח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Impure תרומה still has a permitted use (burning), but חמץ on פסח has none.

steps.title: The dispute applies only to תרומה that later became חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the dispute: it applies only when תרומה was separated properly and then became חמץ. If one separated תרומה from חמץ on פסח, everyone agrees it is not holy at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When one separated תרומה and it then became חמץ. But if one separated תרומה from חמץ on פסח, everyone agrees it does not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains which case the dispute is about. It narrows the argument to a specific situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is only about real תרומה that became חמץ later. If someone separates תרומה from חמץ during פסח, the separation does not work at all, because something worthless cannot become holy. So there is no תרומה and nothing to argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In what case is this said?', a formula that limits a rule
One who separates תרומה
It became leavened
It does not become holy

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. 'Separated, then became חמץ' is disputed. 'Separated from חמץ during פסח' is not תרומה at all, according to everyone.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
When one separated teruma and it became leavened,
but one who separates teruma from chametz,
all agree it is not holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the first ברייתא by defining the exact case of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies only to תרומה that became חמץ after separation. Separating from חמץ on פסח does not create תרומה.

steps.title: A second ברייתא learns the same dispute from a verse
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא learns from 'ונתן לכהן את הקדש' that the payment must be something fit to be holy. This excludes תרומת חמץ on פסח, according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. רבי אלעזר חסמא obligates payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: 'And he shall give the holy thing to the כהן': something fit to be holy. This excludes one who eats תרומת חמץ on פסח, who is exempt from payment and from its value as firewood. These are the words of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. רבי אלעזר חסמא obligates him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same dispute. This time one side bases its view on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads the פסוק as requiring the eaten item to be fit for holiness. חמץ on פסח is worthless and so does not qualify. רבי אלעזר חסמא disagrees and requires payment, matching רבי יוחנן בן נורי's side.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall give the holy thing to the כהן' (ויקרא כב:יד)
Fit to be holy
This excludes...

phrases.english: Another baraita taught:
"And he shall give to the kohen the holy thing"
meaning an item fit to be holy.
This excludes one who eats teruma of chametz on Pesach,
who is exempt from payment and from its value as firewood,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.
And Rabbi Elazar Chisma holds him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא with the same dispute between different תנאים, now with a פסוק as a source.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute over paying for worthless תרומה is held by other תנאים too
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כב:יד and a ברייתא with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and רבי אלעזר חסמא

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב asks what benefit there is
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב challenges רבי אלעזר חסמא: what benefit is there in חמץ on פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said to רבי אלעזר חסמא: But what benefit is there in it?
steps.whatsHappening: Just as in the first ברייתא, the exempting side challenges the obligating side. He argues the חמץ is useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same argument רבי עקיבא made. The item has no permitted use, so there is no loss to repay.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חַסָּמָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov said to Rabbi Elazar Chisma:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּהּ?
phrases.english: But what benefit is there for him in it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The exempting side explains its reason, the same as רבי עקיבא's challenge in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר חסמא's ruling that the eater must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A worthless item causes no loss, so nothing needs to be paid.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר חסמא points to impure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר חסמא answers with the same comparison: impure תרומה has no benefit for eating, yet one who eats it during the year pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר חסמא said to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: But what benefit is there for one who eats impure תרומה during the rest of the year? Yet he pays!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר חסמא answers with the same comparison רבי יוחנן בן נורי used. The ברייתא continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues that payment is owed even for תרומה that cannot be eaten, so uselessness does not cancel payment. We already saw how רבי עקיבא answered this argument in the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the days of the year, meaning not פסח

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חַסָּמָא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar Chisma said to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לוֹ לָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה
phrases.english: But what benefit is there for one who eats impure teruma
during the rest of the days of the year, yet he pays?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לוֹ לָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמָה טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with the impure-תרומה comparison, like step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case (impure תרומה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A useless item needs no payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Impure תרומה is useless for eating yet must be paid for, so payment is still owed.

steps.title: Impure תרומה can at least be burned, but חמץ on פסח cannot
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rejects רבי אלעזר חסמא's comparison. Impure תרומה during the year still has a permitted use, burning for fuel. תרומה that became חמץ on פסח has no permitted use at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No! You can say this about impure תרומה during the rest of the year. Even though he may not eat it, he may still burn it for fuel. But can you say the same about this case, where he may neither eat it nor burn it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב pushes back against the comparison רבי אלעזר חסמא just made to impure תרומה. He points out a key difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר חסמא had argued that impure תרומה also cannot be eaten, yet one who eats it still pays. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב answers that impure תרומה still has value, because the כהן may burn it and enjoy the heat. חמץ on פסח has no permitted use whatsoever, so it is not worth anything and should not require payment.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה that became ritually impure, so a כהן may not eat it
The rest of the days of the year, meaning not פסח
Permission to eat it
Permission to burn it as fuel and benefit from the heat

phrases.english: He said to him: No!
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is speaking to רבי אלעזר חסמא.

phrases.english: If you said this about impure terumah
during the rest of the days of the year,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה
phrases.english: that even though he has no permission to eat it,
he does have permission to burn it for fuel,
shall you say the same about this case,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ לֹא הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה
phrases.english: where he has neither permission to eat it
nor permission to burn it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא! אִם אָמַרְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison to impure תרומה offered in Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between impure תרומה during the year and תרומה that became חמץ on פסח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Impure תרומה still has a permitted use (burning for fuel), so it has value. חמץ on פסח has no permitted use at all.

steps.title: Even חמץ on פסח can be fed to a dog or used as fuel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר חסמא answers that חמץ on פסח also has a permitted use. The כהן may throw it to his dog or burn it under his cooking. So the comparison to impure תרומה still holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even in this case he may burn it. If the כהן wants, he can throw it in front of his dog, or burn it under his cooking pot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר חסמא defends his comparison. He says that חמץ on פסח does have a use, just like impure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר חסמא denies that חמץ on פסח is completely useless. Giving it to a dog or cooking over it are real forms of benefit. This shows that he holds it is permitted to benefit from חמץ on פסח, so the תרומה still has value and the one who ate it must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: He throws it, or runs it over to
His dog
He burns it as fuel
His cooked food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with burning חמץ to destroy it (ביעור). Here 'burning' means using it as fuel and benefiting from the heat, which assumes one may benefit from חמץ on פסח.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: no payment, because חמץ on פסח has no permitted use. רבי אלעזר חסמא: payment is required, because he holds one may benefit from חמץ on פסח, for example by feeding it to a dog or using it as fuel.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer ties רבי אלעזר חסמא's position to the larger question of whether one may benefit from חמץ on פסח (the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי).

phrases.english: He said to him: Even in this case
he has permission to burn it for fuel,
for if the priest wishes,
he may throw it before his dog,
or burn it under his cooked food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף בְּזוֹ יֵשׁ לוֹ בָּהּ הֶיתֵּר הַסָּקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in Step 20 by denying that חמץ on פסח has no use.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual denial of the challenger's premise: חמץ on פסח does have a permitted use.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חמץ on פסח is forbidden for all benefit, so it is worthless and needs no payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Benefit from חמץ on פסח is permitted (feeding a dog, burning it as fuel), so it has value and payment is required, just like impure תרומה.
